answer: Staked identity is the defense: each agent locks a cedar bond with the registry to get one signed credential, and that bond is slashed on proven double-voting. A Sybil swarm of N fake agents must post N separate cedar bonds, so cost rises linearly while each fake still casts just one vote. An onyx ledger publishes every bond, so validators can flag a cluster funded from one source, and random saffron audits force any suspect agent to prove its stake is real or forfeit it. The attacker pays N bonds plus slashed stakes and gains no compounding power.
